title: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor as a biomarker in cancer-related cognitive impairment among adolescent and young adult cancer patients
notes: AYA cancer (15-39yo): breast 24%, head/neck 22%, others. Chemo: platinum 61%, anthracyclines 26%, taxanes 24%. 49% concurrent radiotherapy+chemo. CANTAB battery + FACT-Cog. Linear mixed models adjusted for sociodemographic, baseline cognition, fatigue, psychological distress, time. BDNF measured via ELISA. Baseline BDNF → memory (β=0.05 p=0.018), attention (β=0.04 p=0.029). Post-baseline BDNF → exec function (β=0.04 p=0.030). Also: BDNF Val66Met Met/Met → better exec function vs Val/Val (β=0.82, p=0.012). Anthracycline subgroup: 1 ng/mL BDNF decrease → 0.84-point FACT-Cog total decrease (p=0.014). Cancer patients had much lower BDNF than controls (10.7 vs 21.6 ng/mL, p<0.001).
unmapped_findings: Baseline BDNF → Attention (CANTAB RVP): β=0.04, p=0.029 — no ER_NEUROPLAST_ATTN edge in registry
BDNF Val66Met Met/Met → exec function: β=0.82, p=0.012 — genetic moderator, not an edge
Self-perceived cognitive abilities (PCA): β=0.19, p=0.020 — maps to COGCOMPLAINTS but via BDNF not OIC
